---
title: "tidyselect and across()"
---

## Selectors

Selectors pick columns by name, pattern, or type. They work in `select()`,
`relocate()`, `rename_with()`, `arrange()`, `distinct()`, `group_by()`,
`count()`, `across()`, `pick()`, and the tidyr functions.

| Selector | Columns |
| --- | --- |
| `'x'`, `['x', 'y']` | By name |
| `starts_with('x')`, `ends_with()`, `contains()` | By name fragment; case-insensitive unless `ignoreCase: false` |
| `matches('^x\\d+$')` | By regular expression |
| `num_range('x', 1, 3)` | `x1`, `x2`, `x3` |
| `everything()`, `last_col()` | All columns, the last column |
| `all_of([...])`, `any_of([...])` | Names from a list, strict or lenient |
| `where('numeric')`, `where(fn ($values, $type, $name) => ...)` | By type or predicate |
| `group_cols()` | The grouping columns |
| `except(...)` | Everything but these (dplyr's `-x`) |
| `any_selected(...)`, `all_selected(...)` | Union and intersection |

`where()` accepts `'numeric'`, `'integer'`, `'double'`, `'character'`,
`'logical'`, `'factor'`, and `'date'`, or a `Phibble\Type`.

## across()

`across(cols, fns, names:)` applies functions to several columns inside
`mutate()` or `summarise()`. Grouping columns are never selected. `fns` is one
function or an associative array of named functions. Output names default to
`{col}` for one function and `{col}_{fn}` for several.

{{< include ../examples/_across.md >}}

What each function receives:

- A phplyr helper passed as a first-class callable, such as `mean(...)`, is
  called with the column name.
- In `summarise()`, other closures receive the column's values as a list.
- In `mutate()`, other closures receive one value at a time, or the whole
  column if the first parameter is typed `array`.
- A closure may return a helper's result, as in
  `fn ($v) => mean($v, naRm: true)`, which is then evaluated on the group.

Inside any of these functions, `cur_column()` returns the name of the column
being processed.

`if_any(cols, fn)` and `if_all(cols, fn)` test a predicate across columns, in
`filter()` or as a logical column in `mutate()`. They use R's NA logic, so a
predicate may return null for NA. With no columns selected, `if_any()` is
false and `if_all()` is true, as in dplyr 1.1. `pick(...)` returns the selected columns of the current group
as a table, for use inside closures.
